claims.text: On 50 complex skills, Elevate detects means of 70.67 problems with GPT-4 and 76.67 with DeepSeek, outperforming Vitas and the author-designed chatbots.
claims.quote: These results highlight the effectiveness of Elevate, demonstrating that it significantly outperforms the previous SOTA baselines in detecting weaknesses in VPA applications.

claims.text: Elevate sustains discovery beyond round 10: GPT-4/DeepSeek find 23.33/25.67 additional problems in rounds 10–20, versus Vitas 16.33 and chatbots 0.33/4.00.

metrics.name: additional detected problems between interaction rounds 10 and 20

claims.quote: Notably, between the 10th and 20th interaction rounds, Elevate (GPT4) and Elevate (DeepSeek) identified 23.33 and 25.67 new problems, respectively.

claims.text: Across the three-trial problem union, Elevate GPT-4/DeepSeek uncover 12/16 problems missed by Vitas and both author chatbots.

metrics.name: problems unique to each Elevate implementation

claims.quote: From the results, we observe that Elevate (GPT4) and Elevate (DeepSeek) uncover 12 and 16 unique problems, respectively, which are missed by both Vitas and chatbot-style LLM testers.

claims.text: Elevate identifies 83.7% of the combined observed problem set.

metrics.name: fraction of observed problem union detected

claims.quote: Additionally, Elevate successfully identifies 83.7% of all detected issues, demonstrating its effectiveness in VPA testing.

claims.text: Elevate leads runtime-problem detection across the reported types; GPT-4 finds 8 privacy violations and 7 unstoppable-app issues.

metrics.name: detected problems by runtime problem type

claims.quote: Elevate (GPT4) demonstrates particular strength in uncovering Privacy Violations and Unstoppable App issues, detecting 8 and 7 instances, respectively.

claims.text: Both Elevate implementations find 5 of 6 long-path problems (83.3%), versus Vitas 2 and each author chatbot 1.

metrics.name: detected problems with shortest path longer than six inputs

claims.quote: These results demonstrate that Elevate is notably more capable of discovering hard-to-reach problems in VPA apps.

claims.text: Elevate GPT-4/DeepSeek find 55/59 of 74 problems with high user-input similarity (74.3%/79.7%), versus Vitas 37 and author chatbots 11/22.
claims.quote: Specifically, among the problems with the highest similarity scores, Elevate (GPT4) and Elevate (DeepSeek) detect 74.3% and 79.7%, respectively.

claims.text: Elevate GPT-4/DeepSeek reach 75.7%/78.3% sentence-state coverage, exceeding Vitas 65.1% and both author chatbots below 50%.
claims.quote: The results show that Elevate (GPT4) and Elevate (DeepSeek) achieve the highest coverage, reaching an average of 75.7% and 78.3%, respectively.

claims.text: Elevate GPT-4/DeepSeek reach 81.9%/83.3% semantic-state coverage, approximately 12 percentage points above Vitas and at least 26 points above the author chatbots.

metrics.name: GPT-4-extracted semantic-state coverage against observed-state union

claims.quote: Compared to Vitas, Elevate covers 12% more of the state space than the SOTA non-LLM-based tester.

claims.text: Observer simplification has a smaller state-coverage effect than Generator or Planner simplification, but still reduces coverage.

metrics.name: sentence/semantic state coverage under agent simplification

claims.quote: Compared to the Generator and Planner, the Observer has a relatively smaller direct impact on state coverage.

claims.text: For GPT-4, Generator simplification produces the largest agent-ablation coverage drop, to 56.5% sentence and 61.6% semantic coverage.
claims.quote: For GPT-4, the Generator has the most significant impact on coverage (i.e., removing it, the sentence and semantic rate drop to 56.5% and 61.6%, respectively, which are the lowest in three agents).

claims.text: For DeepSeek, Planner simplification produces the largest agent-ablation coverage drop, to 60.5% sentence and 63.6% semantic coverage.
claims.quote: For DeepSeek, the Planner contributes the most to state coverage and removing it, the sentence and semantic rate drop to 60.5% and 63.6%, respectively.

claims.text: Removing behavior-model prompt information reduces both sentence and semantic coverage by at least 10% in the paper's terminology.
claims.quote:
The results show that removing the behavior model results in at least a 10% decrease in both sentence state cov-
erage and semantic state coverage compared to Elevate.

claims.text: Generator simplification causes the largest problem-detection decline, to no more than 66% of full Elevate's problems; the second control label is corrupted in the text.

metrics.name: detected-problem count relative to full Elevate

claims.quote: Among the components, removing Generator has the largest negative impact on problem detection: w/o Generator(GPT4) and w/o DeepSeek(GPT4) detect no more than 66% of the problems found by Elevate.

claims.text: Planner simplification reduces detected problems by averages of 20 with GPT-4 and 25 with DeepSeek.
claims.quote: Removing Planner has the second largest impact, leading to an average decrease of 20 and 25 problems for GPT-4 and DeepSeek, respectively.

claims.text: Observer simplification reduces detected problems by approximately 20 on average.
claims.quote: Eliminating Observer also reduces problem detection performance, resulting in approximately 20 fewer problems discovered on average.

claims.text: Removing behavior-model prompt guidance reduces detected problems to means of 52.3 with GPT-4 and 51.3 with DeepSeek.
claims.quote: Without the high-level guidance it provides, the problem number of detected problems drops to 52.3 for GPT-4 and 51.3 for DeepSeek.

claims.text: State extraction exceeds 99% agreement with expert-generated states for both models; the reported 95% intervals are [99.0%,99.5%].
claims.quote: The state extraction and transition generation accuracy exceed 99% for both Elevateimplementations.

claims.text: Transition generation exceeds 99% expert-reference accuracy; GPT-4 has a 95% interval of [99.3%,99.7%] and DeepSeek [99.0%,99.5%].

metrics.name: transition accuracy requiring both endpoints to match expert states

claims.quote: The state extraction and transition generation accuracy exceed 99% for both Elevateimplementations.

claims.text: Observer Guidance increases state-extraction accuracy by over 10%; without feedback, GPT-4/DeepSeek achieve 87.4%/88.5%.
claims.quote: Without the feedback mechanism, Observer achieves an average state extraction accuracy of 87.4% and 88.5% on GPT-4 and DeepSeek, respectively.

claims.text: Across 4,000 skills, Elevate GPT-4/DeepSeek detect 3,486/3,541 problems, exceeding Vitas (Table 6: 2,878; prose: 2,876).
claims.quote: We can find that in total 4,000 apps, Elevate (DeepSeek) and Elevate (GPT4) detected 3,541 and 3,486 problems, respectively.

claims.text: In the large dataset, Elevate exceeds 65% sentence-state coverage in most skill categories, while Vitas remains below 55%.
claims.quote: From the results, we observe that Elevate achieves a sentence state coverage of over 65% and a semantic state coverage of over 70% across most categories.

claims.text: In the large dataset, Elevate exceeds 70% semantic-state coverage in most skill categories, while Vitas remains below 60%.

metrics.name: GPT-4-extracted semantic-state coverage by skill category

claims.quote: From the results, we observe that Elevate achieves a sentence state coverage of over 65% and a semantic state coverage of over 70% across most categories.

claims.text: Elevate achieves nearly 30% higher semantic coverage than Vitas in Music, Home, Car and Kids categories; the text does not separate the two model results.
claims.quote: In categories “Music,” “Home,” “Car,” and “Kids,” Elevate exhibits a substantial advantage over Vitas, achieving nearly 30% higher semantic state coverage.

claims.text: Users regard the sampled weaknesses as significant: mean 4.47/5; privacy violations score 4.63 and unstoppable-app issues 4.55.
claims.quote: In summary, the results indicate that users regard all detected weaknesses as both significant and impactful, with Privacy Violation and Unstoppable App issues standing out as particularly severe.

claims.text: Users regard the sampled weaknesses as impactful: mean 4.53/5; privacy violations score 4.72 and unstoppable-app issues 4.63.
claims.quote: In summary, the results indicate that users regard all detected weaknesses as both significant and impactful, with Privacy Violation and Unstoppable App issues standing out as particularly severe.

claims.text: The successful 4,000-skill evaluation is presented as evidence of Elevate's scalability.
claims.quote: In a large-scale evaluation on 4,000 Alexa skills, Elevate further demonstrated 15% higher coverage than Vitas, confirming its effectiveness, scalability, and potential for widespread application in VUI testing.

claims.text: The large-scale results are presented as evidence of potential widespread practical application in VUI testing.
claims.quote: In a large-scale evaluation on 4,000 Alexa skills, Elevate further demonstrated 15% higher coverage than Vitas, confirming its effectiveness, scalability, and potential for widespread application in VUI testing.

claims.text: The authors infer that Elevate's user-like inputs reveal issues more likely to occur during real use; encounter frequency itself is not measured.

metrics.name: annotator-rated similarity to typical user inputs

claims.quote: These findings indicate that Elevate’s behavior more closely resembles that of real users, enabling it to uncover issues that are more likely to be encountered in real-world usage.

claims.text: Unexpected exits constitute the largest share of detected runtime problems on the complex dataset.
claims.quote: Although different testers are used, Unexpected Exit problem accounts for the largest proportion.

claims.text: Most large-dataset problems occur at startup or termination, especially unexpected exits and unstartable apps.
claims.quote: The experimental results indicate that most of the detected problems arise during the startup and termination phases of VPA applications.

claims.text: Elevate occasionally misses unexpected-exit problems found by Vitas or the author chatbots using strange inputs, as illustrated by Amateur Impressions.
claims.quote: However, as these skills usually have difficulty in understanding strange inputs, Vitas and chatbot (LLM) detect the problems (i.e., unexpected exit).

claims.text: Elevate uses means of 9,078 input and 1,282 output tokens per skill, with an estimated GPT-4 cost of $0.13 per skill.
claims.quote: This results in an average cost of approximately 0.13 dollars per skill when using GPT-4.

claims.text: The authors consider the approximately $0.13-per-skill GPT-4 cost reasonable and acceptable given the coverage improvement; user willingness to pay is not evaluated.
claims.quote: Given the significant improvements by Elevate, this cost is reasonable and acceptable.

claims.text: The reported total 4,000-skill costs are $310.5 for DeepSeek and $7.9 for GPT-4, preserving the paper's stated model-to-cost ordering.

metrics.name: total LLM cost for large-dataset trial

claims.quote: When Elevate is implemented with DeepSeek and GPT-4, the total cost to test the Stable-Large-Dataset amounts to 310.5 dollars and 7.9 dollars, respectively.

claims.text: Sentence and semantic coverage vary little across the three trials for the full and ablated configurations.
claims.quote: The variances in semantic and sentence coverage achieved by all testers across the three trials are small, as indicated by the relatively flat box plots.

claims.text: The consistent category-level advantage over Vitas is interpreted as robustness across diverse skill domains.
claims.quote: For other categories, while the improvement of Elevate may not be as substantial as in the aforementioned categories, the results still demonstrate a consistent performance advantage, confirming the robustness of Elevate in VPA testing across diverse skill domains.

claims.text: In My Horoscope, Elevate generates all 12 valid zodiac signs as context-appropriate candidate inputs, unlike Vitas's unrelated candidates.
claims.quote: Elevate correctly generates all 12 zodiac signs (e.g., Aries, Taurus, Gemini) as candidate inputs, ensuring that the test inputs align with the app’s expected behavior.

claims.text: The movie-skill case suggests semantic-state merging improves testing efficiency by reusing history to avoid redundant input selections relative to Vitas.
claims.quote: The Planner learns that “yes” and “action” are invalid inputs, allowing it to avoid redundant selections, improving testing efficiency.

claims.text: In the movie-skill case, adapting input choices using history reveals an unexpected exit that Vitas misses after terminating the dialogue with 'no'.
claims.quote: This strategy ultimately leads Elevate to detect an unexpected exit problem, demonstrating its effectiveness in systematically uncovering hidden issues.

claims.text: An ambiguous backgammon example yields a semantic-state partition that disagrees with the human expert's partition.
claims.quote: Figure17 presents a case where Elevate generates semantic states that differ from those identified by human experts.

claims.text: The authors argue minor state misinterpretations do not affect stability; the ambiguous case has no downstream input-selection effect, but broader stability is not directly measured.

metrics.name: case-specific downstream effect of ambiguous state split

claims.quote: Nevertheless, Elevate’s stability is not affected by minor misinterpretations.

claims.text: Sentence-state coverage is considered less reliable for true behavioral exploration because equivalent outputs can have different wording.
claims.quote: However, VPA skill outputs are not fixed—the same state can have multiple linguistic variations, making this metric less reliable for assessing true coverage.

claims.text: The authors suggest feedback makes interactions more reliable by detecting and correcting hallucinated outputs; a hallucination-specific outcome is not reported.
claims.quote: To mitigate this issue, Elevate employs a feedback mechanism that detects and corrects hallucinated outputs, ensuring more reliable interactions.

claims.text: The authors hypothesize that DeepSeek has stronger logical reasoning and planning than GPT-4 Turbo, explaining model-dependent ablation effects.

metrics.name: model-dependent coverage sensitivity to agent simplification

claims.quote: Compared to GPT-4 Turbo, DeepSeek demonstrates superior logical reasoning and planning capabilities.

claims.text: The authors hypothesize that DeepSeek produces higher-quality candidate input sets than GPT-4; input-set quality is not directly scored.

metrics.name: relative coverage impact of Generator versus Planner simplification

claims.quote: As a result, DeepSeek is able to generate a higher-quality candidate set of inputs.

claims.text: The unusually large gains in Music, Home, Car and Kids are attributed hypothetically to richer LLM domain knowledge.
claims.quote: We hypothesize that LLMs possess richer domain knowledge about these applications.

claims.text: On the 4,000-skill Stable-Large-Dataset, Elevate achieves about 15% higher coverage than Vitas.

metrics.name: sentence/semantic state coverage against the observed-state union

reachability by executing these tests on downstream applications.

claims.text: GPT-4o VulFinder accuracy is 0.81 on Java, 0.80 on Python and 0.80 overall; reported relative gains over Dependabot/TRANSFER are 45%/7% on Java, 67%/33% on Python and 51%/16% overall, with a 21% Java gain over VESTA.
claims.quote:
As shown in Table 2, overall, compared with
the dependency-based analysis tool GitHub Dependabot and the
most popular TRANSFER, VulFinder improves the accuracy by
51% and 16%, and F1-score by 16 % and 36%, respectively.

claims.text: GPT-4o VulFinder F1 is 0.83 on Java, 0.78 on Python and 0.80 overall; reported relative gains over Dependabot/TRANSFER are 15%/14%, 22%/189% and 16%/36%, respectively; Java F1 also exceeds VESTA's 0.59.
claims.quote:
As shown in Table 2, overall, compared with
the dependency-based analysis tool GitHub Dependabot and the
most popular TRANSFER, VulFinder improves the accuracy by
51% and 16%, and F1-score by 16 % and 36%, respectively.

claims.text: Authors claim superiority over all three baselines in recall; VulFinder reports 0.77 Java/0.74 Python/0.76 overall and 33%/363% gains over TRANSFER, but Table 2's Dependabot recall of 1.00 contradicts the all-baseline claim.
claims.quote:
The proposed VulFinder outperforms three state-of-the-art tools
in all three metrics.

claims.text: Dynamic exploit validation in VulFinder reduces false positives relative to dependency-only Dependabot.
claims.quote:
In contrast, tools such as VulFinder,
VESTA, and TRANSFER, which incorporate dynamic validation
with vulnerability exploit generation, have signi ﬁcantly
improved accuracy, indicating a r eduction in false positives.

claims.text: VulFinder generates valid exploits for 22/25 vulnerabilities (88%), compared with VESTA's reported 8/25 (32%) and TRANSFER's 11/25 (44%).

metrics.name: number/proportion of vulnerabilities with a valid generated exploit

claims.quote:
Another evidence is
that VulFinder is able to generate valid exploitable tests for 88 %
(22/25) of the vulnerabilities, while VESTA and TRANSFER are
only 32 % (8/25) and 44 % (11/25), respectively (Table 1).

claims.text: VulFinder generates valid exploit tests for 38 of the 50 reachable downstream applications in Table 1.

metrics.name: downstream applications with valid generated exploit tests

claims.quote:
The experimental vulnerability dataset includes vulnerable packages, vulnerability types, and the number of downstream reachable
applications, along with the results of valid test program generation by VulFinder, VESTA, and TRANSFER.

claims.text: VulFinder demonstrates cross-language generalizability on the evaluated Java and Python datasets.
claims.quote:
Experimental results show the superiority of VulFinder on both
Java and Python datasets.

claims.text: VulFinder is faster than TRANSFER in all three timing cases: HTTPCLIENT-1803 23.2 vs 33.5 s, Zip4J-263 11.3 vs 31.2 s and Python Pillow 10.1 vs 103.2 s; authors report an average efficiency improvement exceeding 1.5 times.
claims.quote:
VulFinder achieves an average ef ﬁciency improvement of over
1.5 times compared to the best performance baseline,
TRANSFER.

claims.text: Removing distillation decreases overall accuracy by 18% (0.80 to 0.66), with reported Java/Python decreases of 15%/21% (0.81 to 0.69; 0.80 to 0.63).

causes overall accuracy, reca l la n dF 1 - s c o r et od r o pb y1 8%,
24%, and 19 %, respectively.

claims.quote:
Table 4 reveals that removing the autoprompting mechanism
causes overall accuracy, reca l la n dF 1 - s c o r et od r o pb y1 8%,
24%, and 19 %, respectively.

claims.text: Removing distillation decreases overall F1 by 19% (0.80 to 0.65), with Java/Python decreases of 15%/27% (Table 4: 0.81 to 0.69; 0.78 to 0.57).
claims.quote:
Table 4 reveals that removing the autoprompting mechanism
causes overall accuracy, reca l la n dF 1 - s c o r et od r o pb y1 8%,
24%, and 19 %, respectively.

resulted in a 28 % decrease in accuracy, a 9 % decrease in recall
and a 20 % decrease in F1-score.

claims.quote:
While removing the discriminator and validator
resulted in a 28 % decrease in accuracy, a 9 % decrease in recall
and a 20 % decrease in F1-score.

claims.quote:
While removing the discriminator and validator
resulted in a 28 % decrease in accuracy, a 9 % decrease in recall
and a 20 % decrease in F1-score.

claims.text: The discriminator and validator filter nontriggerable cases and reduce invalid exploit tests, including tests generated for negative examples.
claims.quote:
Without a discriminator and validator, VulFinder
tends to generate vulnerability test programs indiscriminately,
including for negative examples, leading to a proliferation of
invalid test cases.

claims.text: VulFinder's generation-time efficiency is less affected by programming-language environment than TRANSFER's in the selected cases.
claims.quote:
Despite such factors, VulFinder demonstrates super-
ior time ef ﬁciency and is less affected by variations in program-
ming language environments, consistently outperforming
TRANSFER in terms of time performance.

claims.text: VulFinder's exploit-generation time primarily depends on LLM inference time and API network latency.
claims.quote:
For VulFinder, the time required to generate
vulnerability exploit tests primarily depends on the inference
time of the LLM and the network latency when calling the
API.

claims.text: VulFinder's total generation time is claimed to increase linearly with call-path length; the four-dependency HTTPCLIENT-1803 path is the illustrative case.
claims.quote:
Since VulFinder iteratively processes function call paths
during execution, its total generation time is linearly correlated
with the length of these call paths.

trigger this vulnerability.

claims.text: VulFinder avoids the need to implement a cumbersome, manually specialized inspector to cover mechanisms such as Java SPI.

Since the LLM training corpus contains
implementation mechanisms from multiple languages and code
from popular dependency packages, LLM can fully understand
and cover content beyond the TRANSFER inspector, avoiding the
problem of implementing a cumbersome inspector.

claims.text: The authors recommend practical use of VulFinder to reduce false alarms and missed alarms.

statements, isolating the critical information needed to generate
exploit tests effectively.

claims.text: WebTestPilot's median execution time is 29 seconds per step, faster than LaVague (33s), NaviQAte (40s), and PinATA (38s).
claims.quote:

outperformingLaV ague(33s),NaviQAte(40s), andPinATA(38s).

claims.text: WebTestPilot consumes a median 10k tokens per step, below LaVague's 49k and PinATA's 19k but above NaviQAte's 9k.
claims.quote:

claims.quote:

linearly with the number of steps.

claims.text: Action Execution and Page Reidentification consume 33% and 32% of tokens; Oracle Inference/Symbolization and Page Reidentification consume 34% and 39% of time, making reidentification the principal bottleneck.
claims.quote:

Action Execution (33%) and Page Reidentification (32%), while execution time is primarily spent on
Oracle Inference and Symbolization (34%) and Page Reidentification (39%).

claims.text: The authors attribute efficiency to hybrid action execution avoiding NaviQAte's DOM-ranking rounds and PinATA's multi-agent communication overhead.
claims.quote:
This efficiency stems
from its hybrid action execution design, which avoids both noisy DOM-based multi-round ranking
(NaviQAte) and multi-agent communication overhead (PinATA).

claims.text: The maintenance variant preserves test actions in 39/40 pooled UI-change cases, outperforming XPath (32/40), CSS (33/40), and Playwright (29/40).

(32/40), CSS (33/40), and Playwright (29/40).

claims.text: The authors attribute superior test-flow reachability partly to proposing multiple actions for a single requirement step.

filling multiple form fields).

SoM prompting avoids common DOM-based pitfalls such as iframes, shadow DOMs, and custom
form components.

claims.quote:
